prerequisites: To properly follow and take advantage of the course, it is recommended to have successfully completed 'Tecnología Mecánica', a compulsory subject taught in the first semester of the third year of the Mechanical Engineering Degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Topic 4. Introduction to automation of manufacturing processes and manufacturing systems
Topic 5. Machine tools with numerical control
Topic 6. Bases for programming with numerical control
Topic 8. Basic programming of machine tools with numerical control
Topic 9. Advanced programming of machine tools with numerical control
Topic 10. Automated manufacturing and assembly systems
Topic 11. Competitive aspects of manufacturing systems
teaching_methods: Resolution of exercises, problems, cases and projects
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.8 * Exam Grade + 0.1 * PEC Grade + 0.1 * Laboratory Practice Grade. To compute the PEC grade, the student must have passed the on-site exam and completed the laboratory practices. Passing the on-site exam is essential to pass the subject. Laboratory practices are mandatory for passing the course and are performed only in the June session; their successful completion remains valid for subsequent academic years.
